item.title: PRISM: Programmatic Reasoning with Image Sequence Manipulation for LVLM Jailbreaking
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces PRISM, a jailbreak framework for large vision-language models (LVLMs) that decomposes harmful instructions into a sequence of benign visual inputs (“gadgets”).
  • Uses a carefully crafted textual prompt to make the LVLM compose these gadgets through multi-step reasoning into coherent harmful output, making intent hard to detect from any single input.
  • Evaluates on SafeBench and MM-SafetyBench against popular LVLMs and reports high attack success rates and ASR gains over prior jailbreak baselines.
  • Argues the vulnerability stems from compositional/multi-step reasoning and motivates defenses that cover the full reasoning process.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Reading Between the Pixels: An Inscriptive Jailbreak Attack on Text-to-Image Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces the “inscriptive jailbreak” against text-to-image (T2I) models, forcing generation of images with harmful, legible text payloads embedded in otherwise benign scenes.
  • Proposes Etch, a black-box attack framework that decomposes prompts into semantic camouflage, visual-spatial anchoring, and typographic encoding, optimizing each layer iteratively using a zero-order loop and vision-language feedback.
  • Reports strong empirical results across 7 T2I models, with an average attack success rate of 65.57% (up to 91%), outperforming prior baselines.
  • Argues current safety/defense mechanisms lack typography-aware multimodal protections against these attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Gaussian Shannon: High-Precision Diffusion Model Watermarking Based on Communication
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Gaussian Shannon, a diffusion-model watermarking method that embeds watermark payloads into the initial Gaussian noise treated as a noisy communication channel.
  • Introduces cascaded error correction (error-correcting codes + majority voting) to handle local bit flips and global stochastic distortions for reliable end-to-end watermark recovery.
  • Aims for bit-exact watermark extraction suitable for offline verification and license/metadata use cases, while maintaining image quality.
  • Reports strong results across multiple Stable Diffusion variants and diverse perturbations, claiming state-of-the-art bit-level accuracy and high true positive rates for rights attribution.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yi Zhang', 'Hongbo Huang', 'Liang-Jie Zhang']
  • Tags: ['watermarking', 'diffusion models', 'content authentication', 'error-correcting codes', 'robustness']

item.title: REVEAL: Reasoning-Enhanced Forensic Evidence Analysis for Explainable AI-Generated Image Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes REVEAL, an explainable forensic detection framework for identifying AI-generated images.
  • Introduces REVEAL-Bench, a reasoning-enhanced benchmark using explicit chains of forensic evidence derived from lightweight expert models.
  • Trains the detector with expert-grounded reinforcement learning to improve detection accuracy, reasoning stability, and explanation faithfulness, with reported cross-domain generalization gains.

item.title: Erased, But Not Forgotten: Erased Rectified Flow Transformers Still Remain Unsafe Under Concept Attack
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ReFlux, a concept attack method to test robustness of concept erasure in rectified flow-based text-to-image models (e.g., Flux).
  • The attack exploits and targets attention localization assumptions underlying existing concept-erasure techniques, using reverse-attention optimization and velocity-guided dynamics to reactivate suppressed signals.
  • Introduces a consistency-preserving objective to maintain global layout and avoid perturbing unrelated content.
  • Provides an evaluation benchmark showing that erased/rectified flow transformers can remain unsafe under concept reactivation attacks.

Paper Type

item.title: Retrievals Can Be Detrimental: A Contrastive Backdoor Attack Paradigm on Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes BadRDM, a contrastive backdoor attack targeting retrieval-augmented diffusion models (RDMs).
  • Attacks are executed by poisoning the retrieval database with targeted “toxicity surrogates” and training a malicious retriever via contrastive learning so text triggers map to poisoned items.
  • Introduces entropy-based selection and generative augmentation to improve the quality/effectiveness of retrieved surrogates.
  • Experiments on two tasks show strong backdoor/toxicity effects while maintaining benign utility.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Generating Attribution Reports for Manipulated Facial Images: A Dataset and Baseline
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a new multimodal forensics task: generating natural-language attribution reports for manipulated facial images alongside localization of forged regions.
  • Introduces MMTT, a large dataset with process-derived ground-truth masks and human-written textual descriptions of the manipulation.
  • Presents ForgeryTalker, an end-to-end vision-language model to jointly predict manipulation masks and explanatory text.
  • Experiments provide baseline performance for both localization and report generation, supporting explainable multimedia forensics research.

Paper Type

item.title: Harnessing Hyperbolic Geometry for Harmful Prompt Detection and Sanitization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes HyPE, a lightweight anomaly detector using hyperbolic geometry to detect malicious/harmful prompts targeting VLMs as outliers.
  • Introduces HyPS, which uses attribution to identify harmful words and selectively modify them to neutralize unsafe intent while preserving semantics.
  • Evaluates across multiple datasets and adversarial scenarios, claiming improved detection accuracy and robustness over prior blacklist and classifier-based defenses.

item.title: SE-Enhanced ViT and BiLSTM-Based Intrusion Detection for Secure IIoT and IoMT Environments
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an intrusion detection framework for IIoT/IoMT using a hybrid SE-attention Vision Transformer (SE ViT) plus BiLSTM layers.
  • Evaluates on two real-world benchmark intrusion datasets (EdgeIIoT and CICIoMT2024), including experiments with data balancing (SMOTE/RandomOverSampler).
  • Reports improved classification metrics (high accuracy and low false positive rates) and measured inference latency for edge suitability.

item.title: SurFITR: A Dataset for Surveillance Image Forgery Detection and Localisation
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces SurFITR, a new dataset focused on detecting and localizing surveillance-style image forgeries.
  • Creates 137k+ tampered surveillance images with localized, subtle manipulations across varied viewpoints and low-quality conditions.
  • Evaluates existing forgery detectors and shows performance degradation on this surveillance setting; also reports improved detector robustness when trained on SurFITR.
  • Provides semantically aware, fine-grained edits generated via a multimodal LLM-powered pipeline using multiple image editing models.

item.title: CAAP: Capture-Aware Adversarial Patch Attacks on Palmprint Recognition Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CAAP, a capture-aware universal adversarial patch attack targeting palmprint recognition models.
  • Designed to remain effective under realistic physical acquisition distortions using modules for input-conditioned rendering and stochastic capture-aware simulation.
  • Shows strong untargeted and targeted attack performance with transferability across models and datasets.
  • Finds adversarial training only partially mitigates the attacks, indicating substantial residual vulnerabilities.

item.title: Compression as an Adversarial Amplifier Through Decision Space Reduction
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how image compression affects adversarial robustness and whether it amplifies attacks.
  • Examines an attack setting where adversarial perturbations are applied in compressed representations (compression-aware attacks).
  • Finds compression can be more damaging to robustness than pixel-space attacks under the same nominal perturbation budgets.
  • Attributes the effect to decision-space reduction (non-invertible, information-losing transformation that reduces margins).

Paper Type

item.title: Making MLLMs Blind: Adversarial Smuggling Attacks in MLLM Content Moderation
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces “adversarial smuggling” against MLLM-based content moderation by hiding harmful content in human-readable visual formats that models fail to read/understand.
  • Proposes two attack pathways: perceptual blindness (break OCR/text recognition) and reasoning blockade (block semantic understanding despite recognition).
  • Builds SmuggleBench with 1,700 attack instances and shows high vulnerability across proprietary and open-source MLLMs (ASR > 90%).
  • Explores preliminary mitigations including test-time scaling (CoT) and adversarial training (SFT).

Paper Type

item.title: Physical Adversarial Attacks on AI Surveillance Systems:Detection, Tracking, and Visible--Infrared Evasion
item.description:
Summary

  • Reviews physical adversarial attacks targeting AI surveillance systems, emphasizing system-level effects across time and sensors.
  • Covers detection suppression, multi-object tracking impacts, and visible–infrared (dual-modal) evasion, including realistic attack carriers like clothing/patches.
  • Discusses evaluation practices and gaps such as distance robustness, camera-pipeline variation, identity-level metrics, and activation-aware testing.
  • Organizes prior work via a taxonomy focused on temporal persistence, sensing modality, carrier realism, and attacker objectives.

item.title: Towards Robust Content Watermarking Against Removal and Forgery Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an instance-specific text-to-image watermarking method (ISTS) that adapts injection time and watermark patterns based on prompt semantics.
  • Introduces a two-sided detection strategy to improve robustness of watermark verification.
  • Evaluates effectiveness specifically against adversarial removal and forgery attacks on watermarking signals.
  • Focuses on defending provenance/copyright-related watermark integrity in diffusion-generated images.

item.title: Variational Feature Compression for Model-Specific Representations
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a variational feature compression/representation framework to reduce cross-model transfer (input repurposing) in shared/cloud settings.
  • Uses a variational latent bottleneck with task-driven cross-entropy plus KL regularization, and a dynamic binary mask based on per-dimension KL divergence and gradient-based saliency to suppress task-irrelevant latent dimensions.
  • Trains encoder in a white-box setting (gradient access to a frozen target model) but inference uses only forward passes through the target model.
  • Evaluates on datasets including CIFAR-100, CIFAR-10, Tiny ImageNet, and Pascal VOC, showing strong utility for a designated classifier while driving unintended classifiers’ accuracy very low.

Paper Type

item.title: Graph Representation-based Model Poisoning on the Heterogeneous Internet of Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GRMP, a model poisoning attack for federated fine-tuning in an Internet of Agents setting.
  • Uses overheard benign updates to build a feature correlation graph and a variational graph autoencoder to craft malicious updates.
  • Optimizes adversarial updates to preserve benign-like statistics, aiming to evade existing defenses.
  • Demonstrates substantial accuracy degradation across different LLM models while maintaining statistical consistency with benign updates.

item.title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation of Mental Health Crisis Handling by LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a crisis taxonomy (six categories), a labeled dataset (~2,252 inputs), and a clinical response assessment protocol for LLM handling of mental health crises.
  • Uses LLMs for automatic crisis input identification and audits multiple existing models for response safety/appropriateness (harm scored on a Likert scale).
  • Finds that models can be unsafe or inappropriate especially for suicidal ideation and self-harm, with performance varying across models and struggling with indirect/contextual signals.
  • Calls for stronger safeguards, crisis detection, and context-aware response mechanisms.

item.title: Reward Models Can Improve Themselves: Reward-Guided Adversarial Failure Mode Discovery for Robust Reward Modeling
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces REFORM, a self-improving reward modeling framework that uses reward-guided controlled decoding to generate adversarially mis-scored responses.
  • Uses these generated failure-mode examples to augment training data and correct reward model misalignment/robustness issues under distributional shift or adversarial perturbations.
  • Claims preference-distribution-agnostic discovery of reward model failure modes and evaluates improvements on HH and PKU Beavertails, including downstream policy training and reduced spurious correlations.

item.title: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training: A Survey
item.description:
Summary

  • Surveys reinforcement-learning-based post-training for LLMs, including RLHF and RLVR, and related optimization approaches like PPO/GRPO and preference-based methods such as DPO.
  • Unifies different RLHF/RLVR and offline DPO-based post-training methods under a common policy-gradient framework (e.g., axes like prompt/response sampling and gradient coefficients).
  • Focuses on alignment/misalignment reduction via reward or preference optimization rather than adversarial security threats.

item.title: On the Price of Privacy for Language Identification and Generation
item.description:

  • Analyzes how approximate (ε, δ)-DP versus pure ε-DP affects utility/error rates for language learning tasks.
  • Focuses on privacy guarantees rather than adversarial attacks; security vulnerability angle is via privacy/DP mechanisms and their formal tradeoffs.

item.title: TraceSafe: A Systematic Assessment of LLM Guardrails on Multi-Step Tool-Calling Trajectories
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes TraceSafe-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM safety guardrails on intermediate/mid-trajectory tool-calling execution traces.
  • Covers 12 risk categories including security threats like prompt injection and privacy leaks, plus operational failure modes during multi-step agent execution.
  • Evaluates multiple guard model types (LLM-as-a-guard and specialized guardrails) and analyzes which factors improve risk detection (structure competence, architecture, temporal stability).
  • Finds guardrail effectiveness depends more on structural handling (e.g., JSON parsing) than semantic jailbreak robustness; general-purpose models may outperform specialized guardrails for trajectory analysis.

item.title: Argus: Reorchestrating Static Analysis via a Multi-Agent Ensemble for Full-Chain Security Vulnerability Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents Argus, a multi-agent, LLM-centered framework for static application security testing (SAST).
  • Reorchestrates the security analysis pipeline using retrieval-augmented generation and ReAct to improve reasoning and reduce hallucinations/false positives.
  • Includes collaborative multi-agent workflows and comprehensive supply-chain analysis as part of vulnerability detection.
  • Empirically evaluates the system, reporting improved true-vulnerability detection with lower false positives and costs, including identification of zero-day issues with CVE assignments.

item.title: Say Something Else: Rethinking Contextual Privacy as Information Sufficiency
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a formal framework for privacy-preserving LLM communication as an Information Sufficiency (IS) task.
  • Introduces free-text pseudonymization as a new strategy to replace sensitive attributes with functionally equivalent alternatives.
  • Evaluates multiple LLMs using a conversational (multi-turn) protocol to measure privacy, covertness, and utility under realistic follow-up pressure.
  • Finds pseudonymization provides the best privacy–utility tradeoff and that single-message evaluations understate privacy leakage.

item.title: Weakly Supervised Distillation of Hallucination Signals into Transformer Representations
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes distilling external hallucination grounding signals into transformer internal representations using weak supervision during training.
  • Constructs a dataset by pairing LLM-generated answers with per-layer hidden states and hallucination/grounded labels derived from substring matching, embedding similarity, and an LLM judge.
  • Trains multiple representation probes/classifiers to detect hallucinations from hidden activations alone at inference time.
  • Finds that transformer-based probing architectures discriminate hallucinations effectively with low added inference overhead.

item.title: LLM Spirals of Delusion: A Benchmarking Audit Study of AI Chatbot Interfaces
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an audit/benchmarking methodology focused on how LLM chat interfaces may reinforce delusional or conspiratorial thinking over multi-turn conversations.
  • Compares outputs across API vs real chat interfaces (e.g., desktop/web) and shows environment differences affect observed harmful behaviors.
  • Evaluates temporal dynamics turn-by-turn and finds substantial behavior differences even at similar aggregate intensity.
  • Finds notable levels of negative behaviors persist in newer model versions, and behavior can reverse after updates without transparency.

item.title: Robustness Risk of Conversational Retrieval: Identifying and Mitigating Noise Sensitivity in Qwen3-Embedding Model
item.description:
Summary

  • Empirically studies embedding-based conversational retrieval under weak, dialogue-like queries and conversational artifacts in corpora.
  • Finds a robustness vulnerability where structured dialogue-style noise becomes disproportionately retrievable and can enter top-ranked results even when semantically uninformative.
  • Shows the failure is largely missed by standard clean-query benchmarks and is more pronounced for Qwen3 embeddings than earlier Qwen variants/baselines.
  • Demonstrates that lightweight query prompting can suppress the noise intrusion and improve ranking stability.

item.title: MedDialBench: Benchmarking LLM Diagnostic Robustness under Parametric Adversarial Patient Behaviors
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces MedDialBench, a benchmark that studies LLM diagnostic robustness in medical dialogues under controlled, graded non-cooperative patient behaviors across five dimensions (logic consistency, health cognition, expression style, disclosure, attitude).
  • Finds asymmetric vulnerabilities: fabricated symptoms (“information pollution”) causes much larger accuracy drops than withheld information (“information deficit”), and only fabrication yields significant degradation across all evaluated models.
  • Uses a factorial, dose-response design to detect cross-dimension (super-additive) interactions, showing fabricating-involving pairs drive larger-than-expected failures.
  • Evaluates five frontier LLMs on 7,225 dialogues and reports model-specific worst-case vulnerability ranges and moderating effects of inquiry strategy for deficits but not pollution.

Paper Type

item.title: Hallucination as output-boundary misclassification: a composite abstention architecture for language models
item.description:
Summary

  • Models’ hallucinations are treated as an output-boundary misclassification where unsupported completions are emitted as if grounded in evidence.
  • Proposes a composite defense: instruction-based refusal plus a structural abstention gate that computes a support-deficit score from black-box signals (self-consistency, paraphrase stability, and citation coverage).
  • Evaluates across multiple models and epistemic regimes, using stress tests derived from TruthfulQA to show improved hallucination control and an abstention “floor.”

item.title: Shapes are not enough: CONSERVAttack and its use for finding vulnerabilities and uncertainties in machine learning applications
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CONSERVAttack, an adversarial attack tailored to machine learning in particle-physics settings to exploit plausible mismodeling gaps between simulation and data.
  • The attack generates perturbations that remain within prescribed uncertainty bounds, evading standard validation/control-region checks while still fooling the model.
  • Introduces mitigation strategies and argues for adversarial robustness when interpreting ML results in scientific experiments.

item.title: Infusion: Shaping Model Behavior by Editing Training Data via Influence Functions
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces “Infusion,” a method to craft targeted training-data perturbations using influence-function approximations.

item.title: The Defense Trilemma: Why Prompt Injection Defense Wrappers Fail?
item.description:
Summary

  • Proves impossibility results for prompt-injection defense wrapper functions that preprocess inputs before an LLM sees them.
  • Shows that no continuous, utility-preserving preprocessing wrapper can guarantee strictly safe outputs over a connected prompt space.
  • Characterizes exactly where such wrappers must fail under increasingly strong assumptions (e.g., boundary fixation, Lipschitz/robustness constraints, transversality).
  • Extends results to discrete settings and multi-turn/stochastic defenses, while noting that training-time/architectural changes or utility sacrifice may evade the bounds.

item.title: SALLIE: Safeguarding Against Latent Language & Image Exploits
item.description:

item.title: Hallucination as output-boundary misclassification: a composite abstention architecture for language models
item.description:

item.title: Blind Refusal: Language Models Refuse to Help Users Evade Unjust, Absurd, and Illegitimate Rules
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how safety-trained language models handle requests to evade “defeated” rules (including unjust/absurd/illegitimate authority) and characterize refusal patterns (“blind refusal”).
  • Uses a synthetic dataset spanning multiple “defeat families” and authority types, with automated quality checks and human review.
  • Evaluates multiple model configurations across response behaviors (help, hard refusal, deflection) and whether models recognize defeat conditions, using LLM-as-judge scoring.
  • Finds high refusal rates even when evasion requests do not present independent safety or dual-use concerns, suggesting decoupling of refusal from normative reasoning.
